summary: Elevated 5xx from prolonged chunked uploads causing API gateway backlog and runtime worker starvation
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-13 11:05 UTC we observed a rising 5xx rate on a subset of routes serving FolioAI's dedicated tenancy. Errors were primarily 502/503 from API gateway and upstream runtime connection resets. Impact: customer observed ~18% of requests failing with 5xx over a 50-minute window; some streaming sessions dropped mid-response leading to customer-visible feature regressions. Environment: prod/us-east, dedicated pool for FolioAI. Steps to reproduce: 1) Initiate 50 parallel multipart/chunked embedding uploads with small (2-8KB) chunks and artificially delayed chunk pacing (50-200ms between chunks). 2) Keep connection open until all chunks delivered. 3) Observe gateway accept-queue growth and incremental increase in upstream runtime worker 'stalled-parser' goroutines. Observed logs: - apigw: "accept_queue_depth=512 route=fio-embed status=503 upstream=reset" - proxy: "read_timeout: client stalled during chunked body; backlog=498" - runtime: "worker: stalled_parser_count=34, mem_heap_alloc=7.8GB, goroutine=1720" - autoscaler: "scale_decision: insufficient CPU headroom; recent_p95_latency=820ms" First-response SLA missed for a portion of affected requests. Temporary mitigations: rate limiting on customer route, diversion to warm fallback variant, and mass-reject policy for slow-chunked uploads applied at 11:25 UTC.
comments: 2026-03-13 11:12 UTC - Support (Aisha): Customer reported increased 5xx affecting embedding uploads. Collected traces and forwarded to SRE. Requested immediate mitigation options.

2026-03-13 11:18 UTC - SRE (Marco): Initial metrics show accept_queue latency rising and a correlated increase in 'stalled_parser' workers in runtime. Hypothesis: a pathological client upload pattern holds socket resources while leaving runtime parse tasks blocked, amplifying backpressure to apigw.

2026-03-13 11:26 UTC - Support (Aisha): Applied temporary route-level rate limit (concurrent_uploads=8) and enabled reject-on-slow-body policy. 5xx rate reduced from 18% to ~4% within 6 minutes per dashboards.
2026-03-13 12:05 UTC - Customer (FolioAI contact: Maya Torres): Confirmed partial recovery but requests intermittently hit 5xx during peak bursts. Shared sample client logs and request IDs.

2026-03-13 16:20 UTC - Engineering (SRE): Deployed parser timeout patch (PR#2398) to staging for validation. Observed improved early-reject behavior on slow-chunked bodies without impacting normal traffic.

2026-03-14 08:40 UTC - Engineering (Marco): Hotfix rolled to prod; removed emergency rate limit for FolioAI, replaced with tuned slow-body reject and adjusted apigw accept-queue threshold. Monitoring shows stable 5xx baseline.

investigation_notes: Timeline: 11:05 UTC - first signal in SRE dashboards; 11:18 UTC - support escalation; 11:25 UTC - emergency rate limit applied; 16:20 UTC - staging patch; 08:40 UTC (next day) - prod hotfix roll.

Root cause hypothesis: Slow-chunked client uploads were holding API gateway connections open and causing a head-of-line resource starvation within the serving-runtime's request parsing pipeline. The runtime's parser would block awaiting chunk completion, causing goroutine accumulation and increasing memory retention which amplified autoscaler and worker churn.

Why this manifested as 5xx: With accept_queue growth and many blocked parser workers, the proxy started returning 502/503 when it could not forward to healthy upstreams. Backpressure then caused some runtimes to hit resource thresholds and reset connections, leading to 5xx.

Evidence: Correlation between slow_body_duration metric and accept_queue_depth (pearson r=0.87). Stack samples showed repeated syscall.SIGPIPE and stalled read loops in parser codepath. Heap profiles showed temporary allocations from buffered chunk assembly.
Scope: Affected only dedicated tenancy for FolioAI due to their client pattern (small-chunk, slow-pacing uploads). Other tenants with bulk uploads using standard chunk sizes not impacted.

Workarounds tested: - Route-level concurrent upload limit (reduced incidents but customer throughput constrained) - Divert to fallback variant (increased latency) - Early-reject on slow-body (best balance).
resolution: Deployed parser timeout and early-reject behavior controlled by configuration (runtime flag: slow_body_timeout_ms=1200). Updated API gateway accept-queue thresholds to fail fast earlier for slow uploads and added a route-level policy to surface client-side guidance (recommended chunk size and pacing). Hotfix PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2398. Rollout notes: staged to 10% (staging) -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring checks between waves; observed no regression for normal traffic. Post-incident actions: (1) add automated synthetic test that simulates small-chunk slow uploads against dedicated pools, (2) update runbook to include early-reject and rate-limit playbook, (3) notify Product about potential UI guidance for customers performing bulk embedding uploads.
